summary: Gleason–Lim–Xu determine the connected components of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties at arbitrary parahoric level in the HN-irreducible case, via the p-adic shtuka moduli spaces, specialization maps for v-sheaves and a generic crystalline monodromy argument, with applications to Shimura varieties. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and seventeen findings are recorded against the open-access published text. Lemma 3.2's component formula (E01) and the orbit formulas of Proposition 5.7 and (5.29) for nonnormal reflex fields (E06, E07) are false as printed; Proposition 3.12 and the component descent in §6 inherit the E01 gap (G02). No counterexample to the main theorems is claimed. Not formalised.

items.name: Isocrystal carrier
items.statement: For prime p and perfect characteristic-p domain k, a K=Frac(W(k))-module V with bijective Frobenius-semilinear operator is a WittVector.Isocrystal. Finite dimension is an additional hypothesis, not a field of this class.
items.note: Only the precise pinned carrier/theorem is credited. Specialized API and tests are future acceptance contracts, not certified implementations.

api.name: GLX26.L50.construct
api.statement: Package the K-module and semilinear equivalence.

api.name: GLX26.L50.characterise
api.statement: Read Frobenius bijectivity and semilinearity from the class.

api.name: GLX26.L50.transport
api.statement: Use Frobenius-equivariant linear maps for isocrystal morphisms.

uses.how: Underlying carrier for filtered isocrystals; no higher-rank classification credit.

items.name: Connected-component quotient
items.statement: For any topological space X, ConnectedComponents X is the quotient by equality of connected components, equipped with the quotient topology.
items.note: Only the precise pinned carrier/theorem is credited. Specialized API and tests are future acceptance contracts, not certified implementations.

api.name: GLX26.L51.construct
api.statement: Map x to its connected-component class.

api.name: GLX26.L51.characterise
api.statement: Classes agree exactly when the representatives lie in one connected component.

api.name: GLX26.L51.transport
api.statement: A continuous map induces a continuous map on connected components.

uses.how: The pinned quotient carrier does not justify commutation with arbitrary group quotients.

items.name: Local reductive datum
items.statement: Fix a prime p, L=breve Qp with arithmetic Frobenius phi and inertia I, a connected reductive G/Qp, a geometric conjugacy class {mu}, b in G(L) with [b] in B(G,{mu}), a parahoric group scheme K over Zp and an Iwahori contained in K(Zp). Set breve K=K(breve Zp).

api.name: GLX26.D01.construct
api.statement: Assemble the fields, Frobenius, group, bound and connected parahoric model.

api.name: GLX26.D01.characterise
api.statement: Distinguish K(Zp), K(breve Zp) and the possibly larger facet stabilizer.

api.name: GLX26.D01.transport
api.statement: Transport along a group map extending to the chosen models and carrying b and mu.

uses.how: Common quantified datum; all later local statements explicitly import it.

items.name: Iwahori–Weyl group
items.statement: For D01 choose the maximal L-split torus S over Qp and T=Z_G(S). The Iwahori–Weyl group is N_G(T)(L)/T(breve Zp), with exact sequence X_*(T)_I -> Wtilde -> W0 and affine Weyl subgroup Wa.

api.name: GLX26.D02.construct
api.statement: Form the normalizer quotient using the connected torus parahoric.

api.name: GLX26.D02.characterise
api.statement: Identify translation kernel X_*(T)_I and quotient relative Weyl group.

api.name: GLX26.D02.transport
api.statement: Compare under compatible group maps, base change and adjoint projection.

uses.how: Controls the admissible locus and Levi decomposition.

items.name: Length-zero component sequence
items.statement: For D02 and the chosen alcove, 1 -> Wa -> Wtilde -> pi1(G)_I -> 0 splits by the length-zero subgroup Omega. Bruhat comparison occurs inside one Omega component.

items.name: Special-vertex splitting and Frobenius warning
items.statement: A chosen special vertex identifies Wtilde with X_*(T)_I semidirect W0, but the splitting need not be phi-equivariant. The gradient of the affine phi-action is its linear action.

items.name: Quasisplit Frobenius action
items.statement: For D01, correct the original Frobenius by an adjoint Weyl element so that phi0 preserves the chosen Borel and special vertex; phi0 gives the action on the based root datum of the quasisplit inner form.

api.name: GLX26.D03.construct
api.statement: Construct the adjoint correction and its action on the apartment.

api.name: GLX26.D03.characterise
api.statement: Compare affine phi with based-datum phi0 and its finite-order gradient.

api.name: GLX26.D03.transport
api.statement: Show changing the pinning conjugates the construction without changing invariant classes.

uses.how: Used for rational dominance averages and HN Levi stability.

items.name: Admissible Weyl set
items.statement: For D01–D02, Adm(mu) consists of w in Wtilde satisfying w <= t^lambda for some lambda in W0 times the dominant inertia coinvariant mu-bar. Parahoric admissibility is the corresponding double-coset image.

api.name: GLX26.D04.construct
api.statement: Form the Bruhat lower union of the Weyl-conjugate translations.

api.name: GLX26.D04.characterise
api.statement: Membership preserves the common Kottwitz component.

api.name: GLX26.D04.transport
api.statement: Map the admissible locus through compatible parahoric or group maps.

uses.how: Defines bounds of local models and closed ADLV.

items.name: Algebraic fundamental group and Kottwitz invariants
items.statement: For reductive G, pi1(G)=X_*(T)/Q_G^vee with its Galois action. Distinguish kappa_G:G(L)->pi1(G)_I from the class invariant kappa:B(G)->pi1(G)_Gamma.

api.name: GLX26.D05.construct
api.statement: Construct the coroot-lattice quotient and inertia/global coinvariants.

api.name: GLX26.D05.characterise
api.statement: Identify the torus quotient with its cocharacter lattice; identify pi1 of simply connected semisimple G with zero.

api.name: GLX26.D05.transport
api.statement: Prove naturality under products, central maps and Frobenius.

uses.how: Target of component maps and z-extension reductions.

items.name: Sigma-conjugacy and sigma-centralizer
items.statement: For D01, B(G) is the set of phi-conjugacy classes in G(L), and J_b represents the group of automorphisms of the G-isocrystal defined by b; J_b(Qp)={g:g b=b phi(g)}.

api.name: GLX26.D06.construct
api.statement: Construct the equivalence relation and the automorphism group functor.

api.name: GLX26.D06.characterise
api.statement: Identify phi-conjugate representatives by a specified change of trivialization.

api.name: GLX26.D06.transport
api.statement: Extend structure group, preserving the J_b action on modifications.

uses.how: Supplies commuting actions and Newton classes.

items.name: Newton point and acceptable classes
items.statement: For D01, nu_b is the rational dominant Newton cocharacter; mu^natural is the image in pi1(G)_Gamma and mu^diamond is the finite phi0-average of the dominant inertia average of mu. B(G,{mu}) imposes kappa(b)=mu^natural and nu_b <= mu^diamond.

api.name: GLX26.D07.construct
api.statement: Construct inertia and Frobenius averages in the rational cocharacter space.

api.name: GLX26.D07.characterise
api.statement: Compare Newton and Hodge bounds using the positive coroot cone and equal Kottwitz class.

api.name: GLX26.D07.transport
api.statement: Prove functoriality for products and central/adjoint maps.

uses.how: HN conditions and generic monodromy inequalities.

items.name: Hodge–Newton irreducibility
items.statement: For D01 and b in B(G,{mu}), HN-irreducibility means every coefficient of mu^diamond-nu_b in the basis of absolute simple coroots is strictly positive. Use the quasisplit based root datum; for a torus the condition is vacuous.

api.name: GLX26.D08.construct
api.statement: Define strict positivity with the actual absolute simple coroot basis.

api.name: GLX26.D08.characterise
api.statement: Translate to the equivalent relative condition using Galois-invariant coefficients.

api.name: GLX26.D08.transport
api.statement: Show invariance under ad-isomorphisms and equivalence factor by factor.

uses.how: Hypothesis of the main component theorem.

items.name: Decent representative
items.statement: For D01, b is s-decent for a positive integer s if (b phi)^s=(s nu_b)(p) phi^s with s nu_b integral. This entails compatible descent of b and nu to Qp^s after the specified normalization.

api.name: GLX26.D09.construct
api.statement: Package s>0, the integral cocharacter and the semilinear identity.

api.name: GLX26.D09.characterise
api.statement: Compare the s-fold operator in each algebraic representation with (s nu_b)(p).

api.name: GLX26.D09.transport
api.statement: Enlarge s by a positive multiple and transport by compatible sigma-conjugacy.

uses.how: Produces the finite-field fiber functor and Newton eigenspaces.

items.name: Existence of decent dominant representatives
items.statement: Every sigma-conjugacy class has a decent representative with dominant Newton cocharacter after choosing sufficiently divisible positive s.

items.name: Restriction of scalars local-field reduction
items.statement: The local component statement over a finite F/Qp reduces to that over Qp by restriction of scalars with compatible Frobenius, parahoric, cocharacter orbit and component invariants. No equal-characteristic conclusion follows from this reduction.

items.name: Component Kottwitz coset
items.statement: For D01, define c_(b,mu) pi1(G)_I^phi as the nonempty fiber of (phi-1)kappa(g)=mu-bar-kappa(b). It is an affine coset in pi1(G)_I; a choice identifies it with the invariant group.

api.name: GLX26.D10.construct
api.statement: Construct the affine solution set with its invariant-group torsor action.

api.name: GLX26.D10.characterise
api.statement: Show every ADLV point maps to this fiber by the Kottwitz identity.

api.name: GLX26.D10.transport
api.statement: Transport cosets under group maps and record the translation induced by left multiplication.

uses.how: Prevents silently replacing the natural target by a group.

items.name: Witt affine flag and closed affine Deligne–Lusztig variety
items.statement: For D01, the mixed-characteristic perfect affine flag is LG/L+K. X_mu^K(b) is its reduced perfect subspace cut out by g^-1 b phi(g) in the union of parahoric double cosets indexed by Adm(mu). Here X_mu is the closed admissible union, not one exact stratum.

api.name: GLX26.D11.construct
api.statement: Construct the bounded perfect subfunctor using relative position and descent.

api.name: GLX26.D11.characterise
api.statement: Identify geometric points with the specified admissible double-coset condition.

api.name: GLX26.D11.transport
api.statement: Construct compatible level, product and group-change maps.

uses.how: Geometric object whose connected components are computed.

items.name: Witt affine flag representability and component map
items.statement: For D01 the affine flag is an ind-perfect algebraic space in the established bounded geometry, its connected components identify with pi1(G)_I, and kappa is locally constant.

items.name: ADLV nonemptiness and Kottwitz surjectivity
items.statement: For D01 with [b] in B(G,{mu}), X_mu^K(b) is nonempty and its Kottwitz component map surjects onto c_(b,mu) pi1(G)_I^phi. These are inputs, not consequences of bijectivity.

items.name: Adjoint isomorphism
items.statement: An ad-isomorphism f:G->H is a group morphism carrying centers to centers and inducing an isomorphism G_ad≅H_ad. Bounds, b and reflex fields must be transported along f.

api.name: GLX26.D12.construct
api.statement: Package the centrality and adjoint isomorphism data.

api.name: GLX26.D12.characterise
api.statement: Identify the common simply connected adjoint cover without asserting surjectivity on rational points of every central isogeny.

api.name: GLX26.D12.transport
api.statement: Compose maps and construct compatible parahoric maps.

uses.how: Controls the group-reduction steps.

items.name: Z-extension
items.statement: A z-extension Gtilde->G is a central extension with induced-torus kernel and simply connected derived group of Gtilde.

api.name: GLX26.D13.construct
api.statement: Construct the extension together with the induced-torus presentation.

api.name: GLX26.D13.characterise
api.statement: Use Hilbert90/Shapiro to prove rational-point surjectivity of this extension.

api.name: GLX26.D13.transport
api.statement: Lift cocharacters and acceptable classes, comparing their adjoint images.

uses.how: Reduces the main theorem to simply connected derived group.

items.name: Lifting the bound and acceptable class
items.statement: For a z-extension and b in B(G,{mu}), choose a lifted cocharacter class and a class btilde in B(Gtilde,{mutilde}) mapping to b. Use the fixed-bound bijections with the adjoint B-set.

items.name: Surjectivity of z-extension component cosets
items.statement: For T07 the map c_(btilde,mutilde) pi1(Gtilde)_I^phi -> c_(b,mu) pi1(G)_I^phi is surjective.

items.name: Adjoint comparison of ADLV components
items.statement: For an ad-isomorphism, transported b,mu and corresponding connected parahorics, the square of ADLV connected components and their Kottwitz cosets is Cartesian.

items.name: Simply connected quotient of rational points
items.statement: Define G°=G(Qp)/im(Gsc(Qp)->G(Qp)). Use this normal quotient as written; it is not asserted to be the maximal abelian quotient for arbitrary anisotropic G.

api.name: GLX26.D14.construct
api.statement: Form the normal image quotient with the locally profinite quotient topology.

api.name: GLX26.D14.characterise
api.statement: When Gder=Gsc, use H^1(Qp,Gsc)=1 to identify G° with Gab(Qp).

api.name: GLX26.D14.transport
api.statement: Induce quotient maps from ad-isomorphisms and compare the common simply connected cover.

uses.how: Corrects the overstatement about maximal abelian quotients.

items.name: Rational local group vanishing and open central-isogeny image
items.statement: For simply connected semisimple G/Qp, H^1(Qp,G)=1. A central isogeny of connected reductive Qp-groups has open finite-index image on rational points; it need not be surjective.

items.name: Locally profinite sheaf
items.statement: For a locally profinite space T, underline T on characteristic-p perfectoid spaces sends S to continuous maps |S|->T. For a locally profinite group this is a group v-sheaf.

api.name: GLX26.D20.construct
api.statement: Sheafify the continuous-map functor with its pointwise operations.

api.name: GLX26.D20.characterise
api.statement: For profinite T and algebraically closed perfectoid C, identify underline T times Spa(C,OC) with the continuous-function perfectoid construction.

api.name: GLX26.D20.transport
api.statement: A continuous map T->U induces the corresponding v-sheaf map.

uses.how: Records continuity before torsor quotients.

items.name: Small v-sheaf and its underlying topology
items.statement: A small v-sheaf admits a set-sized perfectoid cover with the stated small relation; its topological space is obtained from geometric points and the presentation quotient topology. A diamond admits a pro-etale equivalence-relation presentation.

api.name: GLX26.D21.construct
api.statement: Construct a small quotient from an allowed atlas and relation.

api.name: GLX26.D21.characterise
api.statement: Compare underlying spaces under atlas refinement.

api.name: GLX26.D21.transport
api.statement: Form fiber products and the permitted group quotients, tracking smallness.

uses.how: The unrestricted class in the source is larger than the applications.

items.name: Topology of a small v-sheaf quotient
items.statement: If F->H is a K-torsor for a locally profinite K and both sheaves are small, |H| is the quotient |F|/K with the quotient topology. The analogous assertion pi0(H)=pi0(F)/K is false without additional hypotheses.

items.name: Component descent needed by the local-shtuka torsors
items.statement: For the actual locally spatial local-shtuka period torsors, compact parahoric quotients and compact Galois descent used in §§3.5,6.2,6.6–6.7, prove component-orbit comparison with sufficient geometric hypotheses. This is an unresolved restricted supplier contract, not the false universal statement of Lemma3.2.

items.name: Locally spatial inverse-limit topology
items.statement: For a cofiltered inverse system of locally spatial diamonds with qcqs transition maps, the underlying space of the limit is homeomorphic to the inverse limit of underlying spaces. The general small-v-sheaf statement in Scholze12.17 supplies only the corresponding bijection without these spatial hypotheses.

items.name: Reduction of a v-sheaf
items.statement: For a v-sheaf F, its scheme-theoretic reduction on perfect Fp-algebras is F_red(Spec R)=F(Spd(R,R)), with adjunction map (F_red)^diamond->F. Representability by a perfect scheme is an additional property.

api.name: GLX26.D22.construct
api.statement: Construct reduction on perfect algebras and the adjunction morphism.

api.name: GLX26.D22.characterise
api.statement: Compare the reduction of a formal model with its reduced perfected special fiber.

api.name: GLX26.D22.transport
api.statement: Prove reduction commutes with the finite limits used in formal-adic diagrams.

uses.how: Identifies the integral shtuka special fiber with an ADLV.

items.name: Formally adic and formally separated morphisms
items.statement: A map F->H is formally adic when its square with the two reduction adjunction maps is Cartesian. A formally closed immersion is a closed immersion that is formally adic; F is formally separated when its diagonal is formally closed.

api.name: GLX26.D23.construct
api.statement: Form the Cartesian reduction condition and the diagonal instance.

api.name: GLX26.D23.characterise
api.statement: Identify uniqueness of formalizations from formal separatedness.

api.name: GLX26.D23.transport
api.statement: Prove base change and composition of formal-adic morphisms.

uses.how: Needed before specialization can descend.

items.name: Specializing v-sheaf
items.statement: A small v-sheaf F is specializing if it is formally separated and v-formalizing: every perfectoid test map v-locally extends from Spa(R,R+) to Spd(R+,R+). Equivalently it is formally separated and v-locally covered by formal Huber pairs.

api.name: GLX26.D24.construct
api.statement: Package the local extensions and formal separatedness.

api.name: GLX26.D24.characterise
api.statement: Use uniqueness to identify competing formalizations.

api.name: GLX26.D24.transport
api.statement: Pull back two specializing objects over a formally separated target.

uses.how: Descent domain for the specialization map.

items.name: Specialization map
items.statement: For a specializing F, sp_F:|F|->|F_red| is obtained by extending a geometric test point to its integral valuation ring and mapping the closed point of its reduction. It is independent of extensions and continuous.

api.name: GLX26.D25.construct
api.statement: Construct the specialization using an integral formalization.

api.name: GLX26.D25.characterise
api.statement: For Spa(A,A+), compute the ideal {a:|a(x)|<1}.

api.name: GLX26.D25.transport
api.statement: Prove the naturality square for morphisms of specializing v-sheaves.

uses.how: Transfers connected components and level-map surjectivity.

items.name: Prekimberlite
items.statement: A prekimberlite is a specializing v-sheaf F whose reduction is represented by a perfect scheme and whose reduction adjunction is a closed immersion. Set F_an=F minus (F_red)^diamond.

api.name: GLX26.D26.construct
api.statement: Package representable reduction and its closed immersion.

api.name: GLX26.D26.characterise
api.statement: Identify the complementary analytic open.

api.name: GLX26.D26.transport
api.statement: Restrict to formal neighborhoods with their corrected reduction.

uses.how: Carrier for smelted pairs.

items.name: Valuative prekimberlite
items.statement: For a prekimberlite F, let SP_F:F->(F_red)^(diamond/circle) be Gleason’s formal specialization morphism. F is valuative when SP_F is partially proper. The formal thickening functor must be constructed, not replaced by its underlying space.

api.name: GLX26.D27.construct
api.statement: Construct SP_F using the formal thickening adjunction.

api.name: GLX26.D27.characterise
api.statement: Express valuativity by extension over enlarged integral valuation rings.

api.name: GLX26.D27.transport
api.statement: Preserve valuativity under the stated partially proper maps and formal neighborhoods.

uses.how: Supplies specializing topology and smelted kimberlites.

items.name: Smelted kimberlite
items.statement: A smelted kimberlite is a pair (F,D) with F a valuative prekimberlite and D an open subsheaf of F_an that is a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond, with D->F partially proper.

api.name: GLX26.D28.construct
api.statement: Package the pair and its partially proper open inclusion.

api.name: GLX26.D28.characterise
api.statement: Restrict sp_F to |D|.

api.name: GLX26.D28.transport
api.statement: Base change along the formal neighborhoods allowed by Gleason4.39/4.42.

uses.how: Exact hypotheses of specialization comparison.

items.name: Kimberlite
items.statement: A prekimberlite F is a kimberlite when (F,F_an) is a smelted kimberlite and sp on the full analytic locus is quasicompact.

api.name: GLX26.D29.construct
api.statement: Specialize the smelted pair to the full analytic locus.

api.name: GLX26.D29.characterise
api.statement: Over affine reduction charts identify quasicompact specialization with spatial inverse-image diamonds.

api.name: GLX26.D29.transport
api.statement: Transport through the formally closed immersions and formal-etale maps with their hypotheses.

uses.how: Local models provide the connected-tube supplier.

items.name: Tubular neighborhood
items.statement: For a smelted pair (F,D) and constructible locally closed S in |F_red|, its tube is F_/S times_F D, using the formal neighborhood. It corresponds to the INTERIOR of sp_D^-1(S), not in general the entire fiber.

api.name: GLX26.D30.construct
api.statement: Construct the formal neighborhood and its analytic fiber product.

api.name: GLX26.D30.characterise
api.statement: Identify the underlying tube with the interior of the specialization inverse image.

api.name: GLX26.D30.transport
api.statement: Compare nested locally closed sets and permitted base changes.

uses.how: Connected tubes are the normality input.

items.name: Constructibly Jacobson diamond
items.statement: A locally spatial diamond D is constructibly Jacobson when its rank-one points are dense in the constructible topology.

api.name: GLX26.D31.construct
api.statement: Package density of rank-one points in each patch-open subset.

api.name: GLX26.D31.characterise
api.statement: Deduce density of a constructible tube in its full specialization fiber.

api.name: GLX26.D31.transport
api.statement: Prove preservation for the stated etale maps, open immersions and surjective maps.

uses.how: Turns connected tubes into connected fibers.

items.name: Rich and topologically normal smelted pair
items.statement: A smelted pair (F,D) is rich if F is valuative, D is constructibly Jacobson, |F_red| is locally Noetherian and sp_D is surjective. A rich pair is topologically normal when every closed-point tube is connected.
items.note: Richness and topological normality are logically distinct properties; a design must expose both predicates and their individual API rather than one opaque combined class.

api.name: GLX26.D32.construct
api.statement: Assemble each finiteness, density and surjectivity hypothesis.

api.name: GLX26.D32.characterise
api.statement: Characterize topological normality by the closed-point tubes.

api.name: GLX26.D32.transport
api.statement: Preserve richness for constructible formal and formal-etale neighborhoods.

uses.how: Hypotheses of the abstract component comparison.

items.name: Rich specialization is a quotient map
items.statement: For a rich smelted pair, sp_D is a quotient map.

items.name: Topologically normal rich specialization compares components
items.statement: For a topologically normal rich smelted pair (F,D), pi0(sp_D):pi0(D)->pi0(F_red) is bijective.

items.name: Bounded de Rham Grassmannian and integral local model
items.statement: For D01, Gr_mu is the closed bounded B_dR affine Grassmannian over breve E, with open Schubert cell Gr_mu^circ. The integral parahoric local model M_K,mu is the v-sheaf closure of this bound in the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian.

api.name: GLX26.D33.construct
api.statement: Construct the bounded generic moduli and integral closure.

api.name: GLX26.D33.characterise
api.statement: Identify generic fiber Gr_mu and reduced special fiber the admissible locus.

api.name: GLX26.D33.transport
api.statement: Construct maps from compatible homomorphisms of parahoric models.

uses.how: Supplies specialization geometry without requiring Satake sheaves.

items.name: Integral local models and unibranch tubes
items.statement: For every reductive G/Qp, parahoric K, geometric bound mu and breve E⊆F⊆Cp as in GLX3.8, the local-model smelted pair has connected tubes. It is a kimberlite; no minuscule restriction is imposed on the tube theorem.

items.name: Minuscule local-model representability
items.statement: For Qp and minuscule mu, the integral local model has the normal flat scheme representative described in §3.2, including the small-p cases supplied by Gleason–Lourenco. Do not import the p>=5 restriction from only the earlier AGLR result.

items.name: Functorial admissible loci
items.statement: A Qp-group morphism extending between chosen parahoric group schemes and carrying mu1 to mu2 induces the affine-flag map, carries the corresponding admissible locus into the target one, and induces a map of closed ADLV for b2=f(b1).

items.name: Criterion for extension to parahoric models
items.statement: Under the parahoric group-model setting of §3.2, the group map extends uniquely when it maps the indicated breve integral points into the target ones, as in Kaletha–Prasad2.10.10.

items.name: Products and determinant at parahoric level
items.statement: Closed ADLV and local-model constructions commute with products for compatible data. A determinant map uses det(K) as the actual level; equality with the full torus parahoric requires a separate proof.

items.name: Local shtuka tower
items.statement: For D01, Sht_(G,b,mu,infty) parametrizes bounded modifications of the prescribed G-bundles with infinite-level trivialization. Finite compact-open levels are quotients with their transition maps; retain commuting G(Qp),J_b(Qp) actions and reflex/Weil descent.

api.name: GLX26.D34.construct
api.statement: Construct the Hecke-fiber moduli with the two trivializations.

api.name: GLX26.D34.characterise
api.statement: Identify level quotient fibers and the infinite-level inverse limit under proved hypotheses.

api.name: GLX26.D34.transport
api.statement: Extend structure group, change levels and compare products with commuting actions.

uses.how: Analytic source of the component computation.

items.name: Integral parahoric shtuka space
items.statement: For D01 and an integral reflex base, Sht_K,mu(b) is the integral bounded shtuka moduli with the parahoric extension data. Its reduction is X_mu^K(b); its generic fiber is the corresponding parahoric-level diamond.

api.name: GLX26.D35.construct
api.statement: Construct bounded integral modifications and the specified Frobenius isogeny.

api.name: GLX26.D35.characterise
api.statement: Compare reduction with the closed admissible ADLV and generic fiber with the tower level.

api.name: GLX26.D35.transport
api.statement: Construct group-map and level-map morphisms before applying specialization.

uses.how: Connects the geometric component theorem to formal models.

items.name: Integral shtukas are rich smelted kimberlites
items.statement: For the datum D01 and the field/base changes specified in §3.3, the integral shtuka with its generic level diamond is a rich smelted kimberlite, with reduced fiber X_mu^K(b) and continuous surjective specialization.

items.name: Tubular local-model correspondence
items.statement: At the corresponding closed points, shtuka and local-model tubes are connected through the diagram of torsors under the connected infinite-dimensional positive Witt loop group in (3.10), giving a bijection of their component sets.

items.name: Shtuka specialization component bijection
items.statement: For D01 and breve E⊆F⊆Cp in the stated complete nonarchimedean setting, specialization induces pi0(Sht_(G,b,mu,K) times Spd F) ≅ pi0(X_mu^K(b)), functorially with the group and level maps.

items.name: Integral group-map specialization square
items.statement: For a compatible map of parahoric models carrying b1,mu1 to b2,mu2, integral shtuka functoriality induces a commuting specialization square with the ADLV map of Lemma3.3.

items.name: Admissible period domain and universal crystalline torsor
items.statement: The Grothendieck–Messing map from Sht_(G,b,mu,infty) to Gr_mu is quasi-pro-etale. Its image Gr_mu^b is the b-admissible open, and the map is the universal G(Qp)-torsor L_b there. Classical finite-extension points pull back to crystalline G-representations with the corresponding bound.

api.name: GLX26.D36.construct
api.statement: Construct the period morphism and its admissible image.

api.name: GLX26.D36.characterise
api.statement: Identify the infinite-level space as the universal torsor over this open.

api.name: GLX26.D36.transport
api.statement: Pull back at a classical point and compare the resulting Galois representation and isocrystal.

uses.how: Transfers generic crystalline monodromy to component stabilizers.

items.name: Geometric connectedness of the admissible period domain
items.statement: For D01, Gr_mu^b times Spd Cp is connected and dense in Gr_mu times Spd Cp. This includes nonminuscule bounds.

items.name: Transitivity on infinite-level components
items.statement: For D01, G(Qp) acts transitively on pi0(Sht_(G,b,mu,infty) times Spd Cp). Retain as the source target; its printed derivation from unrestricted Lemma3.2 is gated by T21/E01.

items.name: Hecke orbit meets every ADLV component
items.statement: For D01, a geometric point lifted to the infinite-level shtuka has a G(Qp) Hecke orbit whose image at parahoric level and then under specialization meets every component of X_mu^K(b).

items.name: Bialynicki–Birula classical-point comparison
items.statement: The BB map Gr_mu^circ->Fl_mu is an isomorphism for minuscule mu. For general mu it still induces the stated bijection on points over finite F/breve E and identifies classical b-admissibility with the weakly admissible flag condition.

items.name: Hodge–Newton decomposability
items.statement: For D01 with [b] in B(G,{mu}), the pair is HN-decomposable if there exists a PROPER phi0-stable standard Levi M containing the Newton centralizer M_nu such that mu^diamond-nu_b is in the nonnegative rational cone of the simple coroots of M. HN-indecomposable means no such proper M exists.

api.name: GLX26.D40.construct
api.statement: Construct a witness proper Levi and the coroot-cone certificate.

api.name: GLX26.D40.characterise
api.statement: Negate existence to obtain HN-indecomposability.

api.name: GLX26.D40.transport
api.statement: Transport the condition under the compatible adjoint and product reductions.

uses.how: Controls the reduction of non-irreducible pairs.

items.name: Hodge–Newton Levi pieces
items.statement: For a decomposable datum with proper standard Levi M and associated P, index the pieces by the phi-stable parabolics Pprime conjugate to P modulo W_K^phi. For each choose h giving the transported Levi Mprime, bound mu_Pprime and b_Pprime=h^-1 b phi(h), with the corresponding parahoric.

api.name: GLX26.D41.construct
api.statement: Construct the parabolic index set and transported data.

api.name: GLX26.D41.characterise
api.statement: Identify the embedding of its ADLV by left multiplication by h.

api.name: GLX26.D41.transport
api.statement: Compare Kottwitz invariants with the translation kappa(h).

uses.how: Open-closed decomposition and coset obstruction.

items.name: Hodge–Newton decomposition
items.statement: For D40, X_mu^K(b) is the disjoint union of the Levi ADLV pieces D41, each embedded as an open and closed perfect subspace, with the indexing and translated data just specified.

items.name: Minimal Hodge–Newton Levi
items.statement: There is a unique minimal phi0-stable standard Levi in the HN decomposition such that its resulting pairs are HN-indecomposable.

items.name: Basic noncentral pairs in an adjoint simple group
items.statement: If G is adjoint Qp-simple, [b] is basic and the Hodge coweight is noncentral, then the acceptable pair is HN-irreducible.

items.name: Indecomposable but non-irreducible alternative
items.statement: For adjoint Qp-simple G and an HN-indecomposable pair, either it is HN-irreducible or mu-bar is central and b is phi-conjugate to t^(mu-bar), with the conventions of Proposition4.7.

items.name: Central-bound discrete ADLV
items.statement: Suppose G_ad is Qp-simple, b is a representative of a basic element of B(G), mu-bar is central and [b] lies in B(G,{mu}). Then X_mu^K(b) is discrete and isomorphic to G(Qp)/K(Zp) as in Proposition4.8, with the required representative normalization.

items.name: Adjoint invariance of HN-irreducibility
items.statement: For an ad-isomorphism and compatible bounds and classes, the source pair is HN-irreducible exactly when the target pair is.

items.name: Product criterion for acceptable and irreducible pairs
items.statement: For G=product G_i, B(G,mu)=product B(G_i,mu_i), and HN-irreducibility holds exactly when it holds for each factor.

items.name: Proper rational Levi has a Kottwitz kernel
items.statement: For adjoint Qp-simple G and a proper rational parabolic with Levi M, pi1(M)_I^phi -> pi1(G)_I^phi is not injective.

items.name: Split torus proves rational coset infinitude
items.statement: If a nontrivial Qp-split torus S in a quasisplit adjoint Qp-simple G is used to test a compact open K, the uniformizer section lambda->lambda(p)K embeds an infinite cocharacter lattice in G(Qp)/K after the boundedness argument. This is a map of sets; G/K is not generally a group.

items.name: Quasisplit component bijection forces HN-irreducibility
items.statement: For D01 with G quasisplit, if the parahoric component Kottwitz map is bijective, then (b,mu) is HN-irreducible.

items.name: Filtered isocrystal
items.statement: For finite K/breve Qp, a filtered isocrystal is a finite-dimensional breve Qp-space with bijective phi-semilinear Frobenius and an exhaustive separated decreasing integer filtration on its K-base change. Morphisms commute with Frobenius and preserve filtration.

api.name: GLX26.D50.construct
api.statement: Construct the finite-dimensional isocrystal and finite filtration.

api.name: GLX26.D50.characterise
api.statement: Compute Hodge degree from graded dimensions and Newton degree from Frobenius slopes.

api.name: GLX26.D50.transport
api.statement: Define tensors, duals and scalar extension with their induced filtrations.

uses.how: Crystalline representation supplier.

items.name: Weak admissibility
items.statement: For D50, weak admissibility requires equality of total Hodge and Newton degrees and the Hodge degree <= Newton degree inequality for every Frobenius-stable subobject with induced filtration.

api.name: GLX26.D51.construct
api.statement: Assemble the total equality and all subobject inequalities.

api.name: GLX26.D51.characterise
api.statement: Check a faithful tensor realization with the theorem’s exact G-structure criterion.

api.name: GLX26.D51.transport
api.statement: Preserve weak admissibility under the admissible tensor equivalence and allowed finite field extensions.

uses.how: Genericity lowers Hodge degrees of subobjects.

items.name: Colmez–Fontaine equivalence
items.statement: Over finite K/breve Qp in the source setting, weakly admissible filtered isocrystals form the exact tensor category equivalent to crystalline Qp-representations via D_cris and V_cris. Preserve the coefficient, completeness and residue hypotheses in the original extension of the theorem.

items.name: Admissible pair with reductive structure
items.statement: For D01 and finite K/breve Qp, a cocharacter mu_eta over K in {mu} defines (V,rho)->(V⊗breve Qp,rho(b)phi,Fil_mu_eta). The pair is admissible when this exact tensor functor lands in weakly admissible objects.

api.name: GLX26.D52.construct
api.statement: Construct the functor from each algebraic representation with its weight filtration.

api.name: GLX26.D52.characterise
api.statement: Test admissibility with the original faithful-representation/tensor criterion.

api.name: GLX26.D52.transport
api.statement: Transport simultaneously b and mu_eta under conjugacy and group maps.

uses.how: Connects the acceptable class to a chosen filtration.

items.name: Triviality of the crystalline fiber-functor torsor
items.statement: For an admissible pair D52 with [b] in B(G,{mu}), the Qp-fiber functor obtained through V_cris is isomorphic to the standard one. A choice produces a continuous G(Qp)-valued crystalline representation xi, unique up to G(Qp)-conjugacy.

items.name: Crystalline Mumford–Tate group
items.statement: For xi from T51, let H be the Zariski closure of its image and MT=H^0 as in GLX. The Tannakian group of the generated representation category is H. Comparing it with MT requires the connectedness justification or passage to the connected component; Chen3.2.2 defines the full H.

api.name: GLX26.D53.construct
api.statement: Construct the algebraic image closure and its identity component.

api.name: GLX26.D53.characterise
api.statement: Describe the full closure by tensor automorphisms of the generated category.

api.name: GLX26.D53.transport
api.statement: Compare under conjugacy and finite extension, retaining the possible component group.

uses.how: The derived containment is a statement about the connected algebraic group.

items.name: Serre–Sen openness for crystalline image
items.statement: For xi as in T51, its image is open in the rational points of its Zariski closure; equivalently its intersection with the identity component is open there. In particular, if MT contains Gder, the image intersects Gder(Qp) in an open subgroup.

items.name: Generated crystalline tensor category and finite-field fiber functor
items.statement: For D52 with b s-decent, form the tensor subcategory generated by its filtered isocrystals, closed under sums, tensors, duals and subquotients. The decent Frobenius supplies Chen’s fiber functor omega_s to Qp^s-vector spaces and its tensor automorphism group MT_cris,s.

api.name: GLX26.D54.construct
api.statement: Construct the generated subcategory and the finite-field fiber functor.

api.name: GLX26.D54.characterise
api.statement: Identify omega_s on the input Rep(G) with ordinary scalar extension when b is decent.

api.name: GLX26.D54.transport
api.statement: Compare the crystalline and etale fiber functors via period rings and their inner-form torsor.

uses.how: Transfers the derived containment from explicit invariant lines.

items.name: Inner-form comparison of crystalline and etale monodromy
items.statement: Under D54, MT_cris,s and the full etale Tannakian group over Qp^s are inner forms, with the period-ring isomorphism of Chen3.3.3. Containment of the normal derived subgroup transfers through the compatible embedding into G.

items.name: Filtration degree and decent invariant lines
items.statement: For nonzero v in V⊗Qp Qp^s and a finite decreasing filtration from mu_eta, deg(v)=max{k:v in Fil^k}. Set d_s(v)=sum_(i=0)^(s-1)deg((rho(b)phi)^i v). The relevant nonzero vectors satisfy rho((s nu_b)(p))v=p^k v and d_s(v)=k.

api.name: GLX26.D55.construct
api.statement: Construct degree on nonzero vectors, or use extended degree +infinity for zero.

api.name: GLX26.D55.characterise
api.statement: Characterize the two equations defining the invariant-line tests.

api.name: GLX26.D55.transport
api.statement: Compare degree under scalar multiplication and the cyclic Frobenius iterates.

uses.how: Chevalley line criterion for the monodromy group.

items.name: Chen invariant-line stabilizer criterion
items.statement: Under D54, MT_cris,s is the subgroup of G_Qp^s stabilizing every line generated by a nonzero vector of D55, in every algebraic representation; tensor powers of a fixed faithful representation and its dual suffice in the source formulation.

items.name: Generic filtration of a representation
items.statement: For a quasisplit reductive G over a characteristic-zero field K, a cocharacter class with finite reflex field E and V in Rep_K(G), intersect the mu-filtrations over Fl_mu(E), then intersect with V⊂V_E. The result is a G-stable decreasing filtration on V. E/K need not be Galois.

api.name: GLX26.D56.construct
api.statement: Construct the intersection of all rational conjugate filtrations.

api.name: GLX26.D56.characterise
api.statement: Characterize it as the largest G-subrepresentation inside the chosen filtration after base change.

api.name: GLX26.D56.transport
api.statement: Compare conjugate bounds using embeddings of E in a common normal closure.

uses.how: Computes the filtration degree at a generic point.

items.name: Generic flag point
items.statement: For the flag variety Fl_mu over its reflex field E, a point Spec Kprime->Fl_mu is generic when its image is the scheme generic point. Kprime may be finite over breve Qp while having sufficient transcendence over the original reflex field.

api.name: GLX26.D57.construct
api.statement: Package a field-valued point with generic scheme image.

api.name: GLX26.D57.characterise
api.statement: Test vanishing of a section at it by vanishing at the generic point of the integral flag variety.

api.name: GLX26.D57.transport
api.statement: Preserve genericity under the simultaneous conjugacy changes in Theorem5.8.

uses.how: Makes all subobject Hodge bounds minimal.

items.name: Generic point realizes the generic filtration
items.statement: For D56–D57, V intersect Fil_(mu_eta)^k(V_Kprime) equals the generic filtration step on V.

items.name: Galois highest-weight orbit decomposition
items.statement: For quasisplit reductive G/K in characteristic zero, irreducible K-representations are indexed by Gamma_K-orbits of absolute dominant weights; their geometric constituents occur with multiplicity one. A general V decomposes into the corresponding isotypic pieces. Over E refine each full orbit into DISTINCT Gamma_E-orbits.

api.name: GLX26.D58.construct
api.statement: Construct the full Galois orbit and its isotypic summand.

api.name: GLX26.D58.characterise
api.statement: Form the rational orbit average and the distinct refined orbit decomposition.

api.name: GLX26.D58.transport
api.statement: Compare field extension using subgroup orbits, without assuming Gamma_E is normal.

uses.how: Corrects the nonnormal-reflex and repeated-orbit formulas.

items.name: Generic filtration highest-weight threshold
items.statement: For D56 and a full Gamma_K orbit O of dominant weights, its isotypic summand is in generic Fil^k iff the lowest-weight pairing with mu is at least k for EVERY distinct Gamma_E-orbit Oprime in O; equivalently use the orbit average of Oprime since mu is Gamma_E-invariant.

items.name: Generic degree bounded by orbit average
items.statement: For the setup of5.8, a nonzero isotypic component v_O has generic degree equal to the minimum of the refined lowest-weight pairings. This minimum is at most their correctly weighted full-orbit average, equal to <w0 lambda, inertia-average(mu)>.

items.name: Frobenius-summed Hodge bound
items.statement: For the decent setup of5.8 and every highest weight lambda occurring in v, d_s(v) <= s <w0 lambda,mu^diamond>.

items.name: Newton lowest-weight inequality
items.statement: For v satisfying the Newton eigenvalue equation of D55, every occurring weight chi has <chi,nu_b>=k/s. Dominance of nu and the lowest-weight bound give <w0 lambda,nu_b> <= k/s.

items.name: HN positivity forces central highest weights
items.statement: If nu<=mu^diamond is HN-irreducible and an antidominant weight eta satisfies <eta,nu> <= <eta,mu^diamond>, then eta pairs to zero with every simple coroot. For eta=w0 lambda this makes the corresponding irreducible representation trivial on Gder.

items.name: Generic weak admissibility
items.statement: For arbitrary reductive G/Qp, b decent with [b] in B(G,{mu}), and a generic mu_eta over finite Kprime/breve Qp, the pair (b,mu_eta) is admissible.

items.name: Generic crystalline derived monodromy
items.statement: Under T61, if (b,{mu}) is HN-irreducible then MT_(b,mu_eta) contains Gder.

items.name: Infinite transcendence of the completed unramified field
items.statement: breve Qp has infinite transcendence degree over Qp.

items.name: Generic flags over finite extensions of breve Qp
items.statement: For a cocharacter flag variety as in §5, there exists a finite extension K/breve Qp with a K-point mapping to its generic point over the original reflex field.

items.name: Existence of open derived crystalline image
items.statement: For arbitrary G/Qp and an HN-irreducible acceptable pair, there exists finite K/breve Qp and a crystalline xi:Gamma_K->G(Qp) with invariants (b,{mu}) such that xi(Gamma_K) intersect Gder(Qp) is open in Gder(Qp).

items.name: Quasisplit converse to generic derived monodromy
items.statement: For quasisplit G and the generic admissible pair of §5, if MT contains Gder then (b,{mu}) is HN-irreducible.
items.note: Place after M01. It is not an input to the forward generic-monodromy implication.

items.name: Quasisplit component and monodromy equivalences
items.statement: For D01 write (1) the Iwahori component Kottwitz map is bijective; (2) the map at the specified parahoric is bijective; (3) the pair is HN-irreducible; (4) some finite K/breve Qp has a crystalline xi of invariants (b,{mu}) whose image intersects Gder(Qp) openly; (5) the geometric infinite-level component set is a G°-torsor under its G(Qp) action. If G is quasisplit, all five conditions are equivalent.

items.name: Main implications: (3)=>(4)=>(5)=>(1)=>(2)
items.statement: For D01 write (1) the Iwahori component Kottwitz map is bijective; (2) the map at the specified parahoric is bijective; (3) the pair is HN-irreducible; (4) some finite K/breve Qp has a crystalline xi of invariants (b,{mu}) whose image intersects Gder(Qp) openly; (5) the geometric infinite-level component set is a G°-torsor under its G(Qp) action. If G_ad has no anisotropic Qp-simple factor, (3)=>(4)=>(5)=>(1)=>(2) holds.

items.name: Main implications: (5)=>(1)=>(2)
items.statement: For D01 write (1) the Iwahori component Kottwitz map is bijective; (2) the map at the specified parahoric is bijective; (3) the pair is HN-irreducible; (4) some finite K/breve Qp has a crystalline xi of invariants (b,{mu}) whose image intersects Gder(Qp) openly; (5) the geometric infinite-level component set is a G°-torsor under its G(Qp) action. If G is arbitrary, (5)=>(1)=>(2) holds.

items.name: Main implications: (3)=>(4)
items.statement: For D01 write (1) the Iwahori component Kottwitz map is bijective; (2) the map at the specified parahoric is bijective; (3) the pair is HN-irreducible; (4) some finite K/breve Qp has a crystalline xi of invariants (b,{mu}) whose image intersects Gder(Qp) openly; (5) the geometric infinite-level component set is a G°-torsor under its G(Qp) action. If G is arbitrary, (3)=>(4) holds.

items.name: Connected components of all parahoric ADLV
items.statement: For every connected reductive G/Qp, every parahoric K and every acceptable HN-irreducible pair (b,{mu}), kappa induces a bijection pi0(X_mu^K(b)) -> c_(b,mu) pi1(G)_I^phi. No quasisplit, tame, minuscule or p>2 hypothesis is added.

items.name: Anisotropic converse fails
items.statement: For an anisotropic adjoint inner form G=GL_1(D) for a noncommutative central division algebra D, b=1 and mu=0, the component map can be bijective while HN-irreducibility fails, so the reverse implication (2)=>(3) is not claimed for arbitrary G.

items.name: Torus infinite-level component torsor
items.statement: For a torus T and [b] in B(T,{mu}), the geometric infinite-level local shtuka is a T(Qp)-torsor over Spd Cp, and its components are the same T(Qp)-torsor.

items.name: Torus finite-level component coset
items.statement: For a torus with its unique connected parahoric Tpar and an acceptable pair, specialization identifies the finite-level component torsor T(Qp)/Tpar(Zp) with the ADLV Kottwitz coset c_(b,mu) pi1(T)_I^phi, equivariantly.

items.name: Lang–Hensel parahoric torsor vanishing
items.statement: For a smooth affine Zp-group scheme with connected special fiber, the etale torsors in the source situation are trivial over Zp: reduce by Hensel to the finite residue field and apply Lang. In particular the connected parahoric torus quotient commutes with Frobenius invariants.

items.name: Adjoint invariance of bounded de Rham geometry
items.statement: For an ad-isomorphism with transported mu and a common reflex base, the closed de Rham Schubert diamonds identify, and their b-admissible opens identify.

items.name: Adjoint contracted-product shtuka comparison
items.statement: For T73, Sht_H is the contracted product Sht_G times^(G(Qp)) H(Qp), with the natural torsor actions.

items.name: Adjoint invariance of the geometric component torsor property
items.statement: For an ad-isomorphism and the corresponding local data, pi0(Sht_G over Cp) is a G°-torsor iff pi0(Sht_H over Cp) is an H°-torsor.

items.name: Z-extension descent of component and HN conditions
items.statement: For a z-extension and lifted data, conditions (1),(2),(3) of M01 hold upstairs iff they hold downstairs.

items.name: Z-extension descent of crystalline openness
items.statement: For the lifted data, condition (4) of M01 holds upstairs iff downstairs, after a finite extension containing the lifted reflex field when necessary.

items.name: Reduction of the main equivalences to simply connected derived group
items.statement: For a z-extension, each of M01’s five conditions is equivalent upstairs and downstairs; thus the implication theorem reduces to Gder=Gsc, preserving quasisplitness and adjoint isotropy conditions.

items.name: Iwahori-to-parahoric ADLV surjectivity
items.statement: For D01 the natural map X_mu^I(b)->X_mu^K(b) is surjective.

items.name: Iwahori component bijection descends to parahoric level
items.statement: For arbitrary D01, condition (1) implies condition (2) of M01.

items.name: Infinite-level component torsor implies finite-level bijection
items.statement: For arbitrary D01, condition (5) implies (1), and hence (2). After Gder=Gsc, det:I->Gab_par is surjective on Zp-points and pi1(G)=X_*(Gab); the component quotient becomes the torus parahoric quotient.

items.name: Finite-field torsor component stabilizer is Galois image
items.statement: For a classical period point y over finite K/breve Qp, the stabilizer of a component of its G(Qp)-torsor is, up to conjugacy, the compact crystalline image xi_y(Gamma_K).

items.name: Derived component stabilizers are open
items.statement: Assume condition (4) over K and pass to any finite extension containing that point. For each component x of the whole infinite-level shtuka over this field, G_x intersect Gder(Qp) is open in Gder(Qp).

items.name: Finitely many sigma-centralizer orbits
items.statement: For bounded mixed-characteristic ADLV at Iwahori level in D01, the J_b(Qp)-orbit set of connected components is finite. The source separately uses local Noetherianity of its underlying topology.

items.name: Component-stabilizer normalizer has finite index
items.statement: In the simply connected derived-group setting of6.7 and under crystalline openness, N_G(Qp)(G_x) has finite index in G(Qp). If every adjoint Qp-simple factor is isotropic it contains Gder(Qp).

items.name: Open derived image gives the geometric component torsor
items.statement: If G_ad has only isotropic Qp-simple factors, condition (4) implies (5).

items.name: Anisotropic adjoint factor component calculation
items.statement: For D01 with Gder=Gsc and G_ad Qp-simple anisotropic, the unique Iwahori I is normal, contains Gder(Qp), and G(Qp)/I≅pi1(G)_I^phi≅Gab(Qp)/Gab_par(Zp). The finite-level period torsor is trivialized by determinant to the torus torsor; its component map is the Kottwitz coset bijection.

items.name: No proper finite-index subgroup in the isotropic simply connected case
items.statement: For semisimple simply connected G/Qp with only isotropic Qp-simple factors, G(Qp) has no proper open subgroup of finite index.

items.name: No proper open normal subgroup in the isotropic simply connected case
items.statement: For semisimple simply connected G/Qp with only isotropic Qp-simple factors, every open normal subgroup of G(Qp) equals the whole group.

items.name: Global stabilizer-parahoric Hodge datum
items.statement: For Corollaries1.5–1.10 fix a Hodge-type Shimura datum (G,X), p>2, G_Qp split over a tame extension, p not dividing |pi1(Gder)|, and Kp a stabilizer-parahoric, with the compatible Hodge embedding and integral models specified in§1.3.

api.name: GLX26.D60.construct
api.statement: Package each global and local hypothesis with the integral model.

api.name: GLX26.D60.characterise
api.statement: Distinguish the connected parahoric equal to a pointwise facet stabilizer from a larger setwise fixer.

api.name: GLX26.D60.transport
api.statement: Change the prime-to-p level through the prescribed tower.

uses.how: Prevents broadening the application hypotheses.

items.name: Tensor-preserving rational quasi-isogeny group
items.statement: For a special point x in either D60 or the PR global Hodge-type datum D62, I_x is the Q-subgroup of (End(A_x)⊗Q)^× preserving all prime-to-p etale tensors and the crystalline tensors in the contravariant Dieudonne module.

api.name: GLX26.D61.construct
api.statement: Construct the simultaneous tensor stabilizer in rational automorphisms.

api.name: GLX26.D61.characterise
api.statement: Compare its local realization with J_b and prime-to-p tensor automorphisms.

api.name: GLX26.D61.transport
api.statement: Transport along a tensor-preserving quasi-isogeny.

uses.how: Group acting in the isogeny-class quotient.

items.name: Perfect tensor-compatible isogeny map
items.statement: Under D60, for each special point x with its b, there is a unique morphism X_(phi mu)^K(b)->S_K,Fbarp^perf lifting the given Siegel isogeny map and preserving the specified crystalline tensors at every geometric point. It is equivariant for Phi(g)=(b phi)^r(g) and the stated geometric r-Frobenius on the target.

items.name: Injectivity of the isogeny-class quotient
items.statement: Under D60 and the extra hypothesis that G_Qp is quasisplit, the isogeny map induces the injective map I_x(Q)\(X_(phi mu)^K(b)(Fbarp) times G(A_f^p))->S_K(Fbarp) at the prime-to-p tower level of Corollary1.6(1). At finite level include the quotient by K^p.

items.name: CM lift in every indicated isogeny class
items.statement: Under D60 and quasisplit G_Qp, the isogeny class parametrized in A02 contains a point lifting to a special (CM) characteristic-zero point.

items.name: He–Rapoport axioms for these integral models
items.statement: Under D60 the He–Rapoport axioms of the cited stratification framework hold for S_K(G,X), with their actual level and Frobenius conventions.
items.note: Source endpoint recorded faithfully, but the named original-source definitions and output diagram are not yet recursively split to declaration size. Partial status is mandatory.

items.name: Almost-product structure of Newton strata
items.statement: Under D60, the Newton strata satisfy the almost-product theorem in Hamacher–Kim Theorem2 after the isogeny map of A01 verifies their AxiomA. Preserve the perfection, Igusa/Rapoport–Zink quotient and coefficient qualifications of that original theorem.
items.note: Source endpoint recorded faithfully, but the named original-source definitions and output diagram are not yet recursively split to declaration size. Partial status is mandatory.

items.name: Normal closure and Siegel closed immersion
items.statement: Under D60 and quasisplit G_Qp, the closure model S_K(G,X)^minus is normal, so normalization is unnecessary and the displayed finite Hodge embedding map to the integral Siegel model is a closed immersion.

items.name: Quasiaffine EKOR strata
items.statement: Under D60, every EKOR stratum in the special fiber of the integral model is quasiaffine.
items.note: Source endpoint recorded faithfully, but the named original-source definitions and output diagram are not yet recursively split to declaration size. Partial status is mandatory.

items.name: Global Hodge-type Rapoport–Zink comparison datum
items.statement: For Corollary6.3 use a tuple (p,G,X,K) of global Hodge type in Pappas–Rapoport§1.3, its model S_K, algebraically closed residue k, x0 in S_K(k), connected parahoric group scheme and the dilated Hodge embedding of§4.5.2. Let RZ_G,mu,x0 be their formal scheme and c:RZ^diamond->M_int the comparison.
items.note: Source endpoint recorded faithfully, but the named original-source definitions and output diagram are not yet recursively split to declaration size. Partial status is mandatory.

api.name: GLX26.D62.construct
api.statement: Construct the PR formal RZ space and its comparison with integral shtukas.

api.name: GLX26.D62.characterise
api.statement: Identify the open-closed immersion and the special-point surjectivity criterion for c to be an isomorphism.

api.name: GLX26.D62.transport
api.statement: Compare Hodge embeddings and prime-to-p levels within PR’s hypotheses.

uses.how: Separate global application context.

items.name: PR uniformization condition from Hecke orbits
items.statement: For D62, the comparison c is surjective on geometric special points and hence an isomorphism of v-sheaves.

items.name: Formal representability of integral local shtukas in global Hodge type
items.statement: For D62, M_int is represented by the formal scheme identified through A08 with RZ_G,mu,x0.

items.name: Isogeny-class p-adic uniformization
items.statement: For D62 and A09, the map I_x0(Q)\(M_G,b,mu times G(A_f^p)/K^p) -> (S_K completed-basechanged to O_breveE) completed along the isogeny class of x0 is the PR4.10.6 uniformization isomorphism of O_breveE-formal schemes, with the precise completion interpretation required by Remark1.13 and RZ6.23.
items.note: Source endpoint recorded faithfully, but the named original-source definitions and output diagram are not yet recursively split to declaration size. Partial status is mandatory.

items.name: Higher-rank Dieudonne–Manin classification
items.statement: Over the algebraically closed residue base of D01, finite-dimensional isocrystals admit their rational-slope decomposition and classification, with the stated Hom and endomorphism division-algebra descriptions. The pin only supplies the carrier and narrower rank-one results.

items.name: Neutral Tannakian reconstruction and fiber-functor twisting
items.statement: For the neutral rigid exact tensor categories used in§5 over characteristic-zero fields, reconstruct the affine group and its representation equivalence; tensor-Isom fiber functors form the relevant torsors and compare the groups by inner forms.

items.name: Generic filtration is Galois-invariant
items.statement: For every τ ∈ Aut(E/K), the generic filtrations attached to μ and to τ(μ) agree: Fil^•_μ V = Fil^•_{τ(μ)} V.
